terms.grammar: passive of efferō, with the ablative of the feeling
evidence: Cic. Sen. 83: efferor studiō patrēs vestrōs videndī (Lewis & Short), s.v. studium
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. efferō: “to be carried away, transported, hurried away” by passions and feelings. The feeling goes into the ablative: studiō, īrā, laetitiā efferrī.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 99, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
